text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Nigerian government may be aiming to boost crude oil output capacity under its "vision 2010" programme to four million barrels per day from 2.5 million and reserves of 40 billion barrles from 25 billion, investigations show.
- About 3.3 billion naira realised from privatisation of state enterprises four years ago is still unutilised.
- Military ruler General Sani Abacha asks for blueprint from water resources ministry for supply of potable water nationwide.
- Electoral commission and political parties agree to delay local council election, compilation of fresh voters' register and delineation of constituences to first quarter of 1997.

- Fresh talks are expected to open in Italy on Monday on how to save a $12 billion sales pact under which Italy's state power firm ENEL was to buy Nigerian liquefied natural gas but which the firm unilaterally cancelled last week.
- Nigerian Ports authority to acquire six dredgers next year in a bid to ensure regular maintenance of ports.

- Petroleum Trust Fund, charged with disbursing money realised from increase in fuel prices, says it has spent more than 32 billion naira on repair of roads nationwide and purchase of drugs for state hospitals.
- Over the counter trading of unquoted securities in the secondary market may be introduced in Nigeria.
- Federal government awards contract to build a jetty for export of coal in southeastern Port Harcourt.
- The Anglican bishop of Niger delta in eastern Nigeria, Rt Rev Samuel Elenwo, was shot in the buttocks by gunmen on Friday but survived the attack.
